explanation: By inclusion-exclusion: 30 + 25 - 15 = 40 students have completed at least one project.

stem: Provide students with a detailed map of their school. Ask them to create an abstract version, highlighting only the main buildings and pathways.
modelAnswer: Abstraction removes unnecessary detail while keeping the information relevant to the task. An abstract school map would retain the main buildings, such as classrooms, the office, and the library, together with the pathways connecting them, while omitting details such as individual trees, benches, or exact building shapes. This mirrors software abstraction, which hides implementation detail behind a simplified view suited to the task.
keyPoints: ["Abstraction means removing unnecessary detail while keeping only the information relevant to the task.","An abstract school map would keep the main buildings (classrooms, office, library) and pathways connecting them, while dropping fine details like individual trees, benches or exact building shapes.","This mirrors how software abstraction hides implementation detail behind a simplified, purpose-relevant view."]

stem: Give students a problem that can be solved with a simple program. Encourage them to write functions to handle different parts of the problem, abstracting complex operations into manageable pieces.
modelAnswer: Breaking a program into functions is an example of modular design. Each function handles one well-defined sub-task. For example, a grade-calculator program can use separate functions to read scores, compute the average, and print the final grade. This makes the overall problem easier to understand, test, and reuse because each function hides the detail of its own sub-task.
